q7.answer: Each API instance polls the config store every 15 s and on startup, and a changed revision number triggers a load. For a new active_version it downloads the artifact, checks the hash, re-runs the feature check, runs a smoke inference, then atomically swaps its in-memory snapshot. The last two active versions stay warm, and a failed load keeps the old version and retries on the next poll.

q8.answer: A separate shadow worker looks up the candidate's own feature set itself, so the candidate's needs never touch the user's request. It applies the same freshness and completeness rule, then runs inference with a 90 ms deadline. Shadow adds no user latency because the API enqueues a small message only after the response is flushed, on a bounded non-blocking queue in a separate service with its own pools. Nothing waits or retries on the request path.

q9.answer: If the queue is full, or a publish is slow or fails, the API drops the message and increments a counter, with no waiting or retry. Workers also mark messages over 60 s old as dropped_stale. Backlog and crashes only reduce pair counts and raise drop rates, which appear in the gate report. The gate applies ceilings on skip and drop rates and a minimum pair count. The ceiling values are not set yet and are an open item.

q10.answer: Workers write a pair record to the shadow results table. It holds request ID, user ID, both item lists, active version, candidate latency, outcome and both source_ts values. An hourly job computes overlap@20, rank correlation on shared items, popular-item share, catalogue coverage and duplicate or unknown-item counts per pair. It aggregates them by day and segment into a report table that a dashboard reads. The daily gate evaluator reads the same results for error rate and p99 latency. This compares list difference and reliability only, not clicks.

q11.answer: At registration the registry runs a feature check. Every required feature must exist in the online store schema and be actually materialized by at least one completed run. Otherwise the stage is blocked_features and the version cannot enter shadow or become active. The check is repeated as a guard when shadow starts, when instances load a version (step 9), at promotion and at rollback. Shadow workers also skip any record lacking the candidate's features. No feature may be removed while the active or rollback-target version needs it.

q12.answer: An on-call engineer runs a rollback operation. It first runs the feature check on the target, then writes the rollback_target, or any previously active version, to active_version in the config store. No 7-day wait or approval is needed. Instances see the new revision on their next poll, within 15 s, and swap to the already-warm previous model with no download. That keeps it well inside 1 minute. If the config write fails, the engineer retries, and as a last resort active_version can be set to none so every request falls back.
